item.title: EU CADA Sovereignty Tiers: What the Four Cloud Levels Mean
item.description:
Key takeaways

  • CADA introduces four cloud sovereignty assurance levels for EU public procurement, each defined by four measurable criteria
  • Member States and EU entities must conduct a sovereignty risk assessment for every cloud use case — it is not optional
  • The compliance requirement cascades: organisations supplying public bodies will face the same questions indirectly
  • The four criteria are specific enough to begin an internal mapping exercise now, before formal guidance is published

The EU’s Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA), proposed on 3 June 2026, introduces four cloud sovereignty tiers for public sector procurement — each defined by a specific set of criteria, each attached to a mandatory risk assessment process. It is the first time the EU has embedded a formal sovereignty classification system directly into procurement law. If your organisation buys cloud from any provider — and the vast majority of European organisations do so from non-EU providers — the tier you sit in is about to become a procurement compliance question, not a strategic preference.
